title: Avatar slider: keep the cheaper slider, or match the original exactly? (2 options)
problem:
The avatar slider under "Start selling" (5 small faces, one slides out about once a second) was rebuilt in our build "st6-rb2" so that it does less work. It looks almost the same, but not exactly, and our near-identical rule (PR-010) can't approve it on its own: with reduced motion on it is not exact, and some differences show only while it moves. Please choose.
Where the numbers come from: frozen frames from the iPhone Simulator's own screen (rendered by the Mac's GPU, not the real phone), each compared to the original with an A-against-A run (P-090, read by mgmt-ops-10). A software snapshot of the same states shows larger differences (max 81 at phone width, 108 at iPad width); that is OBSERVED and not what the screen shows.
idea: Keep st6-rb2's slider (option A), or put the original slider code back (option B).
looksSame: At rest: almost. Phone width: largest shade 50 of 255 on the faces, about 0.03 % of the screen. iPad width: largest shade 36, 0.004 %. With reduced motion on: NOT exact (one face differs where the original's two loads did not differ). In motion: different (see option A).
risk:
- All on-screen numbers are from the Simulator; the real iPhone was not used for the pixel checks.
- Chrome: just after a slide, no pixel differs by more than 8 shades (the largest is 3, below the original's own load-to-load noise of 5; P-086 hold 4b). At 1440 wide, Chrome's own load-to-load noise was too large to judge.
- The phone saving was measured before our "phone checks start warm" rule.

options.name: keep-st6
options.label: A: keep st6-rb2's slider
options.idea: Keep the cheaper slider as it is in our best build.
options.risk:
- Not exact with reduced motion on (see the differences). This does not meet our near-identical rule, which is why you decide.
- The motion differences are small but real; only you can judge them.
- "Try it": A is the original page, B is the whole st6-rb2 build (it has other changes too). Look only at the avatar row under "Start selling".
visualDiff: At rest, phone width (430 CSS px): largest shade 50 of 255 (fill); 126 CSS px² over 4 faces, the largest face 70; about 0.03 % of the screen (0.0315 %). Two loads of the original differ by 0 px. Within our near-identical numbers for a still picture at phone width on the Simulator's screen.

Reduced motion on, phone width: NOT exact. Largest shade 49; 196 CSS px² (largest face 90), 0.05 % of the screen. Two loads of the original already differ there (1,260 device px), but one face (60 CSS px²) differs where the original's two loads did not differ.
At rest, iPad width (1032 CSS px): largest shade 36; 61 CSS px² (largest face 49); 0.004 % of the screen, against 3 loads of each version. Within our near-identical numbers.
In motion: the leaving face is cropped and slides left, where the original narrows in place.
In motion: the original ends each slide with the other faces snapping back 2 px; st6-rb2 has no snap (Chrome measurement).
In motion: the 4th face changes shade slightly as it moves into place (largest shade 45, one face, Simulator screen; OBSERVED, cause unknown). The original shows 0 px there.

gain.how: Measured on an earlier build (aw1-10e) with and without the same slider change: phone Safari Timeline, slider on screen at rest, one session, 2026-10-01. Counts layouts, not slow frames.

gain.how: Scripted scroll test, 4 runs each, one session (phone block S7, 2026-10-02), before the "phone checks start warm" rule.

options.name: match-original
options.label: B: match the original exactly
options.idea: Put the original slider code back. It is the only exact match we have.
options.risk:
- The page-wide layouts at slide starts and the 19-27 slower frames per 20 s at rest are expected to come back (measured on S7's build without the change, not on the original code).
- A halfway build (st6-rb2 with the original's resting values and a narrowing leaver) was not built or tested; whether it would be exact is unknown. If you want it tried, say so in a comment.

gain.what: Page-wide layouts at slide starts and slow frames at rest (iPhone)
gain.before: st6-rb2: about 1 in 36 slides; 0 per 20 s
gain.after: expected back to every slide; 19-27 per 20 s
gain.how: Not measured on the original code: expected from the same two measurements as option A (aw1-10e Timeline, 2026-10-01; phone block S7, 2026-10-02, 4 runs each, one session).

shots.caption: At rest, phone width: original against itself (two loads, 0 px different)

recommended.why: The at-rest saving is measured on the phone, and the still-picture difference is small on screen (within our near-identical numbers at phone and iPad width, though not exact with reduced motion). The motion differences are small but real, and only you can judge them.
